definitionEn: a set of rooms on one floor of a building
example: They rent a small flat near the park.

definitionEn: a very small flat that is mainly one room
example: A studio flat is enough for one student.

definitionEn: a house in a row that shares walls with neighbours on both sides
example: Most streets in that town have terraced houses.

definitionEn: a house with all the rooms on one floor
example: Grandma prefers a bungalow because there are no stairs.

definitionEn: a very tall modern building
example: The new skyscraper has offices on every floor.

definitionEn: the floor of a building at street level
example: The shop is on the ground floor.

definitionEn: the floor above the ground floor (in British English)
example: Our flat is on the first floor.

definitionEn: a machine that carries people between floors
example: Take the lift to the sixth floor.

definitionEn: a set of steps inside a building
example: The stairs are steep in this old house.

definitionEn: the area at the top of a set of stairs
example: The bathroom is on the landing.

definitionEn: the main door into a house
example: Do not leave the front door unlocked.

definitionEn: a door at the back of a house, often to the garden
example: The dog waits at the back door.

definitionEn: a button that makes a sound when a visitor arrives
example: Ring the doorbell twice.

definitionEn: the slot in a door for post
example: The newspaper was stuck in the letterbox.

definitionEn: the covering on top of a building
example: There are solar panels on the roof.

definitionEn: a building for keeping a car
example: Dad parks in the garage when it snows.

definitionEn: land by a house used for plants and sitting outside
example: The children play football in the garden.

definitionEn: an area of short grass in a garden
example: Please do not walk on the wet lawn.

definitionEn: a line of bushes that forms a border
example: A high hedge hides the garden from the road.

definitionEn: a narrow way to walk, for example through a garden
example: The path leads from the gate to the front door.

definitionEn: a covered area at the entrance of a house
example: Leave wet umbrellas in the porch.

definitionEn: the main room where a family sits and watches TV
example: We watch films in the living room.

definitionEn: a room used for eating meals
example: Sunday lunch is in the dining room.

definitionEn: the room where you cook
example: The kitchen window looks onto the garden.

definitionEn: a room with a bed, used for sleeping
example: My bedroom is the smallest room.

definitionEn: a room with a bath or shower and usually a toilet
example: There is only one bathroom in the house.

definitionEn: a bowl you sit on to get rid of waste; a small room for this
example: The toilet is at the end of the hall.

definitionEn: a room used for reading or working at a desk
example: Mum works in the study in the evenings.

definitionEn: a small room for the washing machine and cleaning tools
example: The iron is in the utility room.

definitionEn: a long, soft seat for two or more people
example: The cat sleeps on the sofa.

definitionEn: a big comfortable chair with sides for your arms
example: Grandad always sits in the same armchair.

definitionEn: a low table in front of a sofa
example: Do not put your feet on the coffee table.

definitionEn: a board on the wall or a piece of furniture for books
example: The dictionary is on the top bookshelf.

definitionEn: a table for writing or using a computer
example: My desk is under the window.

definitionEn: a device that gives light
example: Turn on the lamp if you read in bed.

definitionEn: a piece of glass that shows your reflection
example: There is a mirror in the hall.

definitionEn: a small carpet
example: The dog lies on the rug by the fire.

definitionEn: a soft cushion for your head in bed
example: I need a second pillow because my neck hurts.

definitionEn: a large piece of cloth used as a cover on a bed
example: Pull the blanket up if you are cold.

definitionEn: a thick bed cover filled with feathers or similar material
example: A summer duvet is thinner than a winter one.

definitionEn: a large piece of cloth on a mattress
example: Change the sheet once a week.

definitionEn: the thick, soft part of a bed that you lie on
example: This mattress is too soft for my back.

definitionEn: two beds, one above the other
example: The children sleep in bunk beds.

definitionEn: a tall cupboard for hanging clothes
example: Hang your coat in the wardrobe.

definitionEn: a flat board for putting things on
example: The cups are on the kitchen shelf.

definitionEn: a piece of furniture with doors for storing things
example: The plates are in the cupboard.

definitionEn: a box in a piece of furniture that you pull out
example: Keys are in the top drawer.

definitionEn: a machine that washes clothes
example: Do not put trainers in the washing machine.

definitionEn: a machine that dries wet clothes
example: The tumble dryer is next to the washing machine.

definitionEn: a tool that makes clothes smooth with heat; to use it
example: Iron your shirt the night before the concert.

definitionEn: a metal panel on the wall that heats a room
example: Do not dry socks on the radiator.

definitionEn: the part that goes into a wall socket; a stopper in a sink
example: The lamp plug does not fit this socket.

definitionEn: the point in the wall where you connect electricity
example: The socket behind the sofa is free.

definitionEn: the button on the wall that turns lights on or off
example: The light switch is to the left of the door.

definitionEn: a container for rubbish
example: Empty the kitchen bin before it smells.

definitionEn: a container for paper, glass or plastic that will be reused
example: Put bottles in the recycling bin, not the ordinary bin.

definitionEn: a small rug for wiping shoes at the entrance
example: Wipe your shoes on the doormat.

definitionEn: a small metal object that opens a lock
example: I left my key in the door.

definitionEn: a device that keeps a door closed until you use a key
example: The lock on the back door is broken.

definitionEn: a system that makes a loud noise if someone breaks in
example: Set the alarm when you leave the house.

definitionEn: already containing furniture
example: The furnished room includes a bed and a desk.

definitionEn: without furniture
example: An unfurnished flat is cheaper but you need your own bed.

definitionEn: money paid to live in a home you do not own
example: The rent is due on the first of the month.

definitionEn: regular payments for electricity, gas or water
example: The bills are high in winter because of heating.

definitionEn: the area around where you live
example: This neighbourhood is quiet at night.

definitionEn: a part of a town with houses rather than factories
example: A residential area usually has less traffic in the evening.

definitionEn: a small group of houses in the country
example: She grew up in a village with one shop.

definitionEn: a place larger than a village but smaller than a city
example: Our town has a market every Thursday.

definitionEn: a large, important town
example: Warsaw is a busy city.

definitionEn: connected with towns and cities
example: Urban life is noisier than village life.

definitionEn: connected with the countryside
example: Rural buses do not run very often.

definitionEn: making a lot of loud sound
example: The flat is noisy because it is above a bar.

definitionEn: with little noise
example: I need a quiet room to do homework.

definitionEn: to put things in their places and make a room neat
example: Tidy up your bedroom before grandma arrives.

definitionEn: to wash dirty clothes
example: I do the laundry on Sunday evening.

definitionEn: to clean the floor with a vacuum cleaner (British informal)
example: Please hoover the living room before the guests come.

definitionEn: to wipe away the grey powder that collects on furniture
example: Dust the shelves once a week.

definitionEn: to make washed clothes smooth with an iron
example: Dad hates to do the ironing.

definitionEn: to tidy the covers on a bed after you get up
example: Make the bed before you go to school.

definitionEn: to carry rubbish containers outside for collection
example: Take the bins out on Monday night.

definitionEn: to start living in a new home
example: They will move in next Friday.

definitionEn: to leave a home and stop living there
example: The students move out in June.

definitionEn: to sleep in the same bedroom as another person
example: I share a room with my brother.

definitionEn: what you can see from a window
example: The view from the balcony is the river.

definitionEn: the place where something is
example: The location is perfect — five minutes from school.
